title: Dizziness or space motion sickness
summary: Dizziness or a spinning sensation. Onset, intake, fluid losses, movement and mission phase matter. Space motion sickness is only considered if the context supports it (adaptation, head movements); dehydration, if there are fluid losses or low intake. Weakness on one side or impaired speech activates the neurologic card. Informational support only: not a diagnosis or a treatment decision. No clinical personnel on board: the steps are first aid and monitoring; treatment depends on mission procedures.

with_neurologic_signs.text: The dizziness comes with neurologic signs: the neurologic warning signs card applies (emergency).
notify: mission control (if the link is up)

steps.text: Call for emergency help now using the mission's means (ship alarm, crew, mission control if the link is up). Do not wait to see if it gets better.
Note the time the first symptoms started.

assessment.text: Dizziness without neurologic signs: limit movement and monitor.
notify: mission control (if the link is up)

steps.text: Limit head movements; focusing on a task or closing your eyes may ease it.
If weakness on one side, impaired speech or loss of vision appears, treat it as an emergency.

missing_guidance: Motion sickness medication is decided by the mission with its flight surgeon: procedure not loaded in the assistant.

candidates.label: Space motion sickness (space adaptation syndrome)
candidates.minimum_evidence: Dizziness during adaptation to microgravity or related to movement, without neurologic signs.

candidates.label: Dehydration
candidates.minimum_evidence: Dizziness with reported fluid losses (vomiting, diarrhea, sweating) or low intake.
